messages.author: a664004657e4382a
messages.subject: adding covariates
parts:
I’m intending to fit a DSM of marine litter on the sea floor, in my observation field i have (type, size, nature of the bottom, perpendicular distance) within each segment.


In additional I went to add the sources of pollution for my 4 regions (fishing activities, discharge, river, tourism), so how can I enter these variables in my data set in order to use them like covariates, should I make presence/ absence (1,0) for each observation?



THANKS.

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] adding covariates
parts:
Imene

I take it you intend to use the covariates you list in your first paragraph in modelling your detection function and the covariates in the second paragraph as covariates in your dsm model.  Recognise all covariates you include in your dsm model will need to be recorded not only for the survey effort segments, but also for all cells in your prediction grid throughout your study area.  This may be a determining factor in the quality of information you are able to produce for these covariates across the entire study area.  It is also a matter of expert judgement--do you think the amount of tourism influences marine litter on the sea floor, or simply the presents of tourism; those are determinations for you to make.
